title: Hybrid edge->core session economics & latency vignette
body:
Summary:
This is a working vignette exploring a hybrid inference pattern: run a small quantized core on edge (NVidia T4-like instance or small on-prem GPU) for the first n tokens, then transparently offload longer tail tokens to core data-center GPUs. Goal: reduce cost per interactive session while bounding p95 latency for short sessions. This doc captures microbenchmarks, rough cost model, ascii charts, and recommended knob values for a single plausible 8-turn conversational workload.

Motivation / use-case:
- Interactive product with many short sessions (~60% <= 32 tokens total) and a long-tail of verbose sessions (10% > 512 tokens).
- Customers want lower unit cost without regressing the experience for the majority of users.
- Hybrid edge->core offload could reduce per-session compute spend by doing ~70-90% of small sessions entirely on cheaper edge nodes.

Bench outline (hardware/software):
- Edge: 8GB GPU with int8-quantized Llama2-7B variant (runtime build q8x-int8), 16B KV-cache disabled for edge runs; throughput tuned for 1 concurrent session per GPU slot.
- Core: A100-simulated cluster using FP16 kernels and batch size up to 8, standard KV caching.
- Model: Llama2-7B-v2 tuned variants: edge-q8x and core-fp16. Same tokenizer, same seed for sampling.
- Workloads: 10k synthetic sessions sampled from production token distribution (summary of distribution below).
- Offload policy: threshold at token count 48; sessions predicted to exceed 48 tokens are allowed to warm and offload at token 64. Fallback timeout: 250ms for edge-to-core handoff.

Key numeric results (aggregates):
- Session mix: short (0-32t) 60%, med (33-128t) 30%, long (>128t) 10%.
- Average tokens per session: 46.
- Average wall latency for short sessions (edge-only): p50=45ms, p95=120ms, p99=240ms.
- Average end-to-end latency for medium sessions (edge warm + core finish): p50=180ms, p95=420ms, p99=980ms.
- Long sessions (core dominant): p50=320ms, p95=750ms, p99=1800ms.
- Cost per 1k sessions (raw compute only, normalized USD): edge-only: $6.2 per 1k; core-only: $23.4 per 1k; hybrid observed: $9.8 per 1k (weighted mix).

Text chart: percent sessions served on edge vs core by session length:
0-32 tokens  : [##########################] 60% served edge
33-128 tokens: [##################] 30% partial edge then offload  (40% of these complete on core)
>128 tokens   : [----------##########] 10% core dominant

Latency vs cost tradeoff table (per-1k sessions):
Mode        | p95 latency median | compute $/1k 
edge-only   | 120ms              | $6.2
core-only   | 750ms              | $23.4
hybrid (policy A)| 420ms         | $9.8

Observations:
- Hybrid reduces cost by ~58% vs core-only while increasing p95 latency modestly vs edge-only for the subset that offloads.
- Offload handoff contributes a median extra 60-90ms overhead (serialization + network + core scheduling). Handshake failures (~0.6%) cause fallbacks and increase p99 for affected sessions.
- Quantization on edge introduces small output variance (measured BLEU/ROUGE-ish proxy: -0.6% quality delta vs core FP16 for the sampled prompts). For many UIs this is acceptable; for high-quality generation it may not be.

Sensitivity tests (short summary):
- Offload threshold: raising threshold to 96 tokens shifts 12% of med sessions to edge-only, lowering cost to $8.5/1k but increases edge GPU utilization and p95 for short sessions by ~10-15%.
- Offload timeout tuning: reducing handshake timeout to 100ms reduces p95 spikes but increases fallback rate and slightly increases cost (more core replays).

Operational notes:
- Need robust tracing of session affinity and offload events in Console (add timeline markers: edge-start, offload-requested, offload-accepted, core-start, core-finish).
- Rollout plan: run hybrid policy behind feature flag, route 5% traffic, monitor p95 and fallback rate for 48h, increase to 25% if p99 < 2x baseline.

Open questions / risks:
- Security: Are tokens or context chunks encrypted end-to-end during offload? Customer expectations for private deployments will vary.
- Predictors: Can we implement a cheap per-session predictor (based on prompt length + user history) to avoid unnecessary offloads? Early tests reduce offloads by ~8%.
- Billing: How to present hybrid metering to customers (edge compute vs core compute)? Need billing mapping and transparent logs.

Action items / next steps:
- (Evan) Wire up offload trace markers in runtime (ENG-8742) — ETA 1 week.
- (Priya) Run longer A/B at 10% live traffic with real prompts, collect quality deltas — ETA 2 weeks.
- (Mateo) Draft cost allocation for billing UI + examples for customers — ETA 2 weeks.
- (Asha) Prepare a short internal one-pager for sales to explain hybrid benefits and limitations — ETA 3 days.

Appendix: quick methodology notes:
- Cost model used list-price GPU-minute normalized: edge slot cost = $0.0026/min, core GPU cost = $0.012/min. We include only GPU minute amortized compute (exclude networking and infra overhead).
- Synthetic sessions sampled from production session token histogram (anonymized).
- All timings measured end-to-end wall time from request sent to final token emitted; sampling used deterministic seeds to reduce variance.

This doc is intentionally experimental and rough — aim is to capture early signal and recommend a small controlled rollout. Feedback welcome.
